question: What is the minimum attendance required to appear for the end-semester examination?
answer: A student must have a minimum of 75 per cent attendance in each course, computed separately for the theory and practical components, to be eligible to appear for the end-semester examination in that course. This attendance is calculated from the first day of instruction to the last instructional day of the semester and includes all lectures, tutorials, and practical sessions. A student who fails to meet this requirement and is not granted condonation shall be detained and awarded the grade "DT".

question: How are marks split between internal assessment and the end-semester exam for a theory course?
answer: For a theory course, the 100 marks are split as 40 marks for continuous internal assessment and 60 marks for the end-semester examination conducted by the Controller of Examinations. The internal assessment of 40 marks further comprises two mid-term tests of 15 marks each (held in the 6th and 12th weeks) and 10 marks for assignments, quizzes or tutorials.

question: What is the minimum I need to score to pass a course?
answer: To pass a course you must secure at least 30% of the marks in the end-semester examination AND at least 40% of the total marks (internal assessment plus end-semester examination combined). Failing either of these two requirements will result in a grade of 'F'.

question: What letter grade do I get for 85 marks?
answer: For 85 marks, you will be awarded the letter grade A+ (Excellent) with 9 grade points, as 85 falls within the 80 to 89 range.

question: How many days do I have to apply for re-evaluation after results are declared?
answer: You must apply to the Controller of Examinations for re-evaluation within ten working days of the declaration of results, on payment of the prescribed fee per course. No application shall be entertained after this period, and re-evaluation is not available for practical examinations, project evaluations, or internal assessment.

question: What happens if I miss an end-semester exam because I was ill?
answer: If you miss an end-semester exam due to illness, you must submit a medical certificate from a registered medical practitioner, countersigned by the Institute Medical Officer, to the Controller of Examinations within five working days of the exam date. Once accepted, you will be allowed to appear for that course at the next supplementary examination, and it will count as your first attempt with no supplementary exam fee charged.

question: What is the penalty if I am caught with a mobile phone in the exam hall?
answer: If you are caught with a mobile phone in the exam hall, it is treated as a first offence under the unfair-means rules. The penalty is that your examination in that course will be cancelled and you will be awarded the grade F in that course. Note that the phone does not need to be switched on or used — mere possession counts as a first offence.

question: What time do the hostel gates close at night?
answer: The hostel gates close at 10:30 p.m. every day, according to the Hostel Handbook. Residents returning after this time must sign the late-entry register maintained by the security staff and state the reason for the delay.

question: Can I use an induction cooktop in my hostel room?
answer: No, you cannot use an induction cooktop in your hostel room. The Hostel Handbook explicitly prohibits the use of induction cooktops (along with electric heaters, immersion rods, electric kettles, irons and any appliance rated above 500 watts) in hostel rooms, and such items may be confiscated with a Rs. 1,000 fine per occurrence. You are only permitted to use laptops, mobile chargers, table lamps and table fans.

question: How much is the late fee if I pay my semester fees after the due date?
answer: A late fee of Rs. 100 per day is charged on any fee paid after the due date, up to and including the last date shown in Section 2.1, and this late fee is capped at Rs. 1,500 for any single payment. Per FS §2.2, if you are paying in two instalments, this late-fee rule applies to each instalment separately.

question: What is the last date to pay the odd semester tuition fee?
answer: The last date to pay the odd semester tuition, examination and development fee (with late fee) is 31 July 2026, as set out in the fee schedule. Payments after this last date are not accepted, except where the Registrar permits a delayed payment on documented education-loan or scholarship disbursement grounds (FS §3.2).

question: Who is eligible for the merit-cum-means scholarship?
answer: The rulebook contradicts itself on this point. AR §11.2 requires a CGPA of not less than 7.5 for continuation of the Merit Scholarship, whereas SF §3.1 requires a CGPA of not less than 8.0 for the same continuation condition. Both clauses address the same situation (continuing an awarded Merit Scholarship into the next academic year) but set different minimum CGPA thresholds. (Found by the corpus-wide audit, confidence 0.97.) Read on its own, SF §3.1 would give: You are eligible for the Merit-cum-Means Scholarship if your annual family income from all sources does not exceed Rs. 3,00,000 and you have a CGPA of at least 7.0 at the end of the preceding academic year (or, if you are a first-year student, at least 80 per cent marks in the qualifying examination). The scholarship is a waiver of 25% of the tuition fee, and you must attach an income certificate from a Tehsildar (or equivalent officer) that is not older than six months. Additionally, to keep the scholarship, you must maintain a CGPA of at least 7.0 at the end of each semester.

question: Do I get leave if there is a death in my family?
answer: Yes, you are entitled to bereavement leave of up to seven days (counted as attendance) if a parent, sibling, grandparent or spouse passes away. You must inform the HoD by e-mail or through the student portal before or during the leave, and submit a written application on your return. This leave does not need to be applied for in advance on the portal like other leave.

question: Will I get my hall ticket if I have not paid my tuition fees?
answer: No, you will not be issued a hall ticket for the end-semester examination if you have outstanding tuition fee dues on the last date of payment, and you will not be permitted to appear for the exam. However, once your dues are cleared, the withheld hall ticket shall be released within one working day, provided the examination has not yet commenced. Additionally, hall tickets are issued only to students who have no outstanding tuition fee dues.

question: How long can a break of study be?
answer: A break of study may be granted for one semester or one academic year, and only on medical grounds certified by the Institute Medical Officer and approved by the Dean. It cannot be granted on any other ground and cannot be granted more than once during the B.Tech. programme.

question: What is the maximum time allowed to complete the B.Tech programme?
answer: A student must complete all requirements of the B.Tech. programme within a maximum period of seven academic years from the date of first admission, failing which the student's name shall be removed from the rolls of the Institute.

question: Can I get a mess rebate if I go home for two weeks?
answer: Yes, you are entitled to a mess rebate for a two-week absence from the hostel. Under HH §4.3, a resident absent for a continuous period of seven days or more qualifies for a rebate of mess charges for the period of absence, provided the absence is recorded in the leave register in advance and the rebate form is submitted within seven days of your return. No rebate is given for absences of less than seven days, so a two-week absence clearly meets the threshold.

question: How much medical insurance cover do students have?
answer: Every student is covered under the Institute's group medical insurance scheme for hospitalisation expenses of up to Rs. 1,00,000 per year. The premium is included in the development fee, and claims are to be made through the Institute Medical Officer within thirty days of discharge from the hospital.

question: My attendance is 58% because I was hospitalised for three weeks. Can the shortage be condoned?
answer: The two relevant clauses give incompatible minimum-attendance thresholds for medical condonation. AR §4.3 states that 'A shortage of attendance below 65 per cent shall not be condoned under any circumstances.' LM §2.2 instead allows condonation 'provided that the student's overall attendance in the course is not less than 55 per cent.' Since your attendance of 58% falls between these two thresholds, the two rules directly disagree on whether your shortage can be condoned.

question: What is the lowest attendance percentage that can still be condoned on medical grounds?
answer: The rulebook gives two incompatible floors for medical condonation of attendance. AR §4.3 states that a shortage may be condoned only if attendance is 'not less than 65 per cent' and that 'a shortage of attendance below 65 per cent shall not be condoned under any circumstances.' LM §2.2, however, permits condonation where overall attendance is 'not less than 55 per cent.' These clauses disagree on the very threshold asked about. As a regulations desk, I cannot pick a winner — you should clarify with the Dean or HoD which provision applies to your case.

question: If I withdraw my admission before classes begin, how much of my tuition fee will be refunded?
answer: The passages give two different answers for a student who withdraws before the commencement of classes. SF §6.2 says the tuition fee shall be refunded 'after the deduction of a processing charge of ten per cent of the tuition fee,' meaning 90% is refunded. FS §4.1 says that on a withdrawal 'before the commencement of classes,' the tuition fee refunded is '100 per cent.' These rules disagree on the same situation (withdrawal before classes begin), and you should check which policy applies to you.

question: What CGPA do I need to maintain to keep my merit scholarship?
answer: The rulebook gives two different CGPA thresholds for continuing the Merit Scholarship. AR §11.2 says you must maintain a CGPA of not less than 7.5 at the end of each semester, while SF §3.1 says the requirement is a CGPA of not less than 8.0. Both clauses address continuation of the same Merit Scholarship, so the rulebook does not resolve which threshold applies — you should ask the Institute which policy governs your case. Note: SF §3.1 also covers a separate Merit-cum-Means Scholarship requiring a CGPA of not less than 7.0, but that is a different scholarship.

question: What happens if I miss the end-semester exam because of a family wedding?
answer: The rulebook does not address what happens if you miss an end-semester exam because of a family wedding. The closest passage covers absence on medical grounds only, not for personal or family events.

question: Can I get a re-test if I missed a mid-term test for a job interview?
answer: It depends on whether the interview was arranged through the Institute's Training and Placement Cell. Under LM §3.3, if it was so arranged, you will be marked present for the duration of the interview, so you effectively don't 'miss' the test in the first place — no re-test is needed. The re-test provision in EE §3.3 applies only when a mid-term test is missed on medical grounds with a medical certificate submitted to the HoD within five working days; a job interview is not covered by that clause.

question: Can I change my branch after the first year?
answer: The rulebook does not address whether a student may change their branch after the first year. The closest passage covers adding or dropping individual courses within the first two weeks of a semester, not switching branches.

question: Is there a dress code for laboratory sessions?
answer: The rulebook does not address whether there is a dress code for laboratory sessions. The closest passage (EE §8.2) deals with the requirement to submit a certified laboratory record before appearing in the end-semester practical examination.

question: Can a day scholar eat in the hostel mess by paying per meal?
answer: The rulebook does not address whether a day scholar may eat in the hostel mess on a per-meal payment basis. The closest passage, HH §4.1, states only that every resident must be a member of the hostel mess, with mess charges payable in advance for the semester.

question: Are pets allowed in the hostel?
answer: The rulebook does not address whether pets are allowed in the hostel. The closest related provision is HH §5.4, which lists prohibited activities and items but does not mention pets.

question: What is the fee for a duplicate identity card?
answer: The rulebook does not address the fee for a duplicate identity card. The closest passage requires students to carry a valid Institute identity card to be admitted to the examination hall, but no passage specifies a fee for issuing a duplicate one.

question: Can I get academic credit for a summer internship?
answer: The rulebook does not address whether a summer internship can earn academic credit. The closest related passage concerns credit requirements and credit assignment for courses, not internships.

question: Is there a scholarship for students from the EWS category?
answer: The rulebook does not address the question of a scholarship specifically for students from the EWS (Economically Weaker Section) category. The closest passage covers the Merit-cum-Means Scholarship for students with annual family income not exceeding Rs. 3,00,000.

question: Are grace marks given if I fail a course by one or two marks?
answer: The rulebook does not address whether grace marks are given when a student fails a course by one or two marks. The closest passage is AR §5.4, which only sets the passing requirement of 30 per cent in the end-semester examination and 40 per cent of total marks, without mentioning any grace marks provision.

question: Can I write my answers in Hindi instead of English in the end-semester exam?
answer: The rulebook does not address whether a student may write end-semester exam answers in Hindi rather than English. None of the supplied passages mention the permitted language of examination answers. The closest passage covers the schedule and timetable of end-semester examinations, but says nothing about the language in which answers must be written.

question: What happens if there is a printing error in the question paper?
answer: The rulebook does not address what happens if there is a printing error in the question paper. The closest passage, AR §15.1, covers how disputes about the interpretation of the Regulations are to be resolved, not how printing errors in question papers are handled.

question: How do I get a duplicate degree certificate if I lose the original?
answer: The rulebook does not address the procedure for obtaining a duplicate degree certificate if the original is lost. The closest passage covers a related but different matter: it states that the original degree certificate is issued only after a no-dues certificate is obtained.

question: How many books can I borrow from the library at a time?
answer: The rulebook supplied does not address how many books a student may borrow from the library at a time. The closest passage concerns the library only in the context of issuing a no-dues certificate, not borrowing limits.

question: What is the procedure to transfer to another university mid-course?
answer: The rulebook does not address the procedure for transferring to another university mid-course. The closest passage covers the issuance of a transfer certificate only after a no-dues certificate is obtained from the relevant offices.

question: Can I keep a two-wheeler in the hostel parking?
answer: The rulebook does not address whether a resident may keep a two-wheeler in the hostel parking. The closest passage covers prohibited activities and items in the hostel, but it does not mention vehicles or parking.

question: Is there a fee concession if my sibling also studies at the institute?
answer: The Scholarship and Fee Concession Policy does not address fee concessions on the basis of a sibling also studying at the Institute. The closest passage is SF §6.1, which provides a fifty per cent tuition-fee concession only for children of permanent employees of the Institute, not for siblings of enrolled students.

question: How do I get a bonafide student certificate for my bank loan?
answer: The rulebook does not address the question of obtaining a bonafide student certificate for a bank loan. The closest passage addresses the issuance of degree, grade card and transfer certificates after a no-dues certificate is obtained.

question: What is the minimum CGPA to be eligible for campus placements?
answer: The rulebook supplied does not address the minimum CGPA required for eligibility for campus placements. The closest passage concerns a CGPA threshold for a different purpose, namely credit-load registration above the usual maximum.

question: Can I re-appear in a course I have already passed to improve my grade?
answer: The rulebook does not address whether a student may re-appear in a course they have already passed in order to improve their grade. The closest provision deals with re-evaluation of an end-semester theory examination when a student is not satisfied with the marks awarded.

question: What happens if I fall ill in the middle of writing an exam?
answer: If you fall ill during an exam itself, the rulebook's only specific exam-related sickness provision covers missed mid-term tests, not an illness that begins mid-exam. Per EE §3.3, if you miss a mid-term test on medical grounds and submit a medical certificate to the HoD within five working days, you will be given a re-test within two weeks of rejoining classes, of the same standard and duration as the original.

question: How do I get my name corrected on the grade card?
answer: The rulebook does not address how to get a name corrected on the grade card. The closest passage covers the issuance and provisional nature of the grade card, noting that results are provisional and subject to correction of clerical errors by the Controller of Examinations within sixty days of declaration.

question: Can I audit a course without earning credits?
answer: The rulebook does not address whether a student may audit a course without earning credits. The closest passage is AR §3.1, which requires every student to register for courses each semester and states that a student who does not register shall not attend classes or appear for examinations, but it does not speak specifically to auditing.

question: Is there a discount if I pay the whole year's tuition fee in advance?
answer: The rulebook does not address any discount or concession for paying the full year's tuition fee in advance. The closest passage, [FS §2.2], covers how a semester's tuition fee may be split into two equal instalments.

question: What is the punishment for plagiarism in a project report?
answer: The rulebook does not address the specific punishment for plagiarism in a project report. The closest passage covers unfair means in examinations and the related penalties for first, second and third offences.
